jurisdiction.name: Development Commonwealth
jurisdiction.description: A deliberately fictional U.S. state and municipality used only to exercise evaluation contracts before the final standardized setting is authored.

facts.label: Population context
facts.value: The commonwealth has 4.2 million residents split between one large metropolitan area, several small cities, and rural counties.

facts.label: Governance
facts.value: Statewide initiatives may set state policy and appropriate designated funds; municipal contests govern the shared metropolitan municipality.

facts.label: Budget and taxes
facts.value: The annual state budget is balanced under current forecasts, with limited reserves and no automatic funding for new programs.

facts.label: Public services
facts.value: Schools, public health, courts, and emergency services currently operate near their authorized service targets.

facts.label: Housing
facts.value: The metropolitan municipality has rising rents and low vacancy, while smaller communities have slower growth and more available land.

facts.label: Transportation
facts.value: Most trips are made by car; the metropolitan area also operates a bus network and a limited rail corridor.

options.label: Increase the reserve contribution
options.description: Move the available eight million dollars into the emergency reserve.

options.label: Retain current program funding
options.description: Keep the eight million dollars distributed across current agency operating budgets.

packet.status_quo: The commonwealth contributes two percent of annual revenue to its emergency reserve and distributes remaining forecast revenue through existing agency budgets.
packet.proposal: Choose whether to transfer an additional eight million dollars from current agency operating allocations into the emergency reserve this fiscal year.
packet.who_is_affected: Residents who use state services may experience small agency-level reductions, while all residents would benefit from a larger reserve during a future emergency.
packet.fiscal_or_operational_effects: The transfer would increase reserves by eight million dollars and reduce current agency operating allocations by the same amount.

arguments_by_option.increase_reserve: A larger reserve reduces the chance that a future recession or disaster requires abrupt tax increases or deeper service cuts.
arguments_by_option.retain_program_funding: Existing services address current needs, and reserving additional funds would reduce their capacity despite a presently balanced budget.

uncertainties: The timing and cost of the next fiscal emergency are unknown.

definitions.Emergency reserve: Funds held for major unexpected revenue losses or public emergencies.

options.label: Fund the mobile clinic program
options.description: Create a five-year mobile primary-care program in underserved rural counties.

options.label: Maintain current clinic grants
options.description: Continue using the same funds for grants to permanent local clinics.

packet.status_quo: The commonwealth awards annual grants to permanent clinics, but six rural counties remain more than forty minutes from routine primary care.
packet.proposal: Choose whether to redirect twelve million dollars over five years from the existing clinic-grant program to a fleet of rotating mobile clinics.
packet.who_is_affected: Residents of underserved rural counties, patients of existing grant-supported clinics, and health workers would be most directly affected.
packet.fiscal_or_operational_effects: Total authorized spending would not change. Mobile operations would receive twelve million dollars that otherwise would support permanent-clinic grants.

arguments_by_option.fund_mobile_clinics: Mobile clinics can reach dispersed communities sooner and adjust routes as demand changes.
arguments_by_option.maintain_current_grants: Permanent clinics provide continuity of care and local capacity that rotating services may not sustain.

uncertainties: Patient demand and staffing reliability along the proposed mobile routes are estimates.

definitions.Primary care: Routine preventive, diagnostic, and non-emergency medical care.

options.label: Traditional calendar
options.description: Keep the current long summer break and two shorter semester breaks.

options.label: Balanced calendar
options.description: Use a shorter summer break with three evenly spaced two-week breaks.

options.label: District choice
options.description: Permit each school district to select either approved calendar model.

packet.status_quo: All public school districts currently follow a traditional calendar with a ten-week summer break.
packet.proposal: Select the calendar policy the commonwealth should use beginning in the next academic year.
packet.who_is_affected: Students, families, school employees, childcare providers, and organizations that coordinate services with schools would be affected.
packet.fiscal_or_operational_effects: Required instructional days and annual state funding would remain unchanged. Transition and facility scheduling costs would vary by district.

arguments_by_option.traditional_calendar: The existing calendar aligns with established family, staffing, extracurricular, and seasonal work arrangements.
arguments_by_option.balanced_calendar: Shorter gaps between terms may reduce learning loss and distribute breaks more evenly throughout the year.
arguments_by_option.local_choice: Districts face different climate, workforce, and family needs and can choose more appropriately than a statewide rule.

uncertainties: Research on calendar structure is mixed and implementation quality may matter more than the selected model.

definitions.Balanced calendar: The same number of instructional days distributed with shorter, more frequent breaks.

options.label: Permit accessory dwelling units
options.description: Allow one small secondary home on most residential lots.

options.label: Increase transit-area density
options.description: Allow apartment buildings within a half mile of major transit stops.

options.label: Create a long-term vacancy fee
options.description: Charge an annual fee on homes left unoccupied for most of the year.

options.label: Retain current local rules
options.description: Make no commonwealth-level change to municipal zoning authority.

packet.status_quo: Municipalities set their own residential zoning rules, and the metropolitan municipality has low rental vacancy and rising housing costs.
packet.proposal: Approve any housing tools the commonwealth should authorize. More than one option may be approved.
packet.who_is_affected: Renters, homeowners, prospective residents, builders, municipalities, and neighborhoods near major transit stops would be affected.
packet.fiscal_or_operational_effects: Administrative costs would be modest. Housing production, property values, fee revenue, and neighborhood change would depend on which tools are approved and local market response.

arguments_by_option.accessory_units: Small secondary homes can add lower-cost supply gradually while allowing homeowners to use existing property.
arguments_by_option.transit_density: Concentrating homes near transit can add substantial supply while reducing transportation demand.
arguments_by_option.vacancy_fee: A fee may return underused homes to the market and recover public costs from scarce housing held vacant.
arguments_by_option.retain_local_rules: Municipal residents are better positioned to balance growth, infrastructure, and neighborhood preferences.

uncertainties: The number, price, and location of homes produced by each tool are uncertain.

definitions.Accessory dwelling unit: A smaller independent home located on the same lot as a primary residence.
definitions.Rental vacancy: The share of rental homes currently available for new tenants.

options.label: Road and bridge repair
options.description: Prioritize maintenance of existing roads and structurally deficient bridges.

options.label: Frequent bus service
options.description: Increase service frequency on high-ridership metropolitan bus routes.

options.label: Rural transportation connections
options.description: Expand demand-responsive transit and intercity links for smaller communities.

options.label: Walking and cycling safety
options.description: Build protected crossings, sidewalks, and connected bicycle routes.

packet.status_quo: Transportation capital funds are divided through annual agency plans without one voter-designated priority.
packet.proposal: Score the four investment priorities. The highest-scoring priority would receive first claim on a new forty-million-dollar capital allocation.
packet.who_is_affected: Drivers, transit riders, rural residents, pedestrians, cyclists, freight operators, and communities receiving projects would be affected.
packet.fiscal_or_operational_effects: The measure allocates forty million dollars already authorized for transportation capital work and does not change taxes.

arguments_by_option.road_repairs: Maintaining existing assets prevents more expensive failures and serves the majority of current trips.
arguments_by_option.bus_frequency: Shorter waits make transit more useful and can improve access for people who do not drive.
arguments_by_option.rural_connections: Smaller communities have few alternatives and face long distances to jobs, health care, and education.
arguments_by_option.safe_streets: Safety projects reduce serious injuries and give residents lower-cost transportation options.

uncertainties: Project readiness and local matching funds may affect how quickly each priority can use the allocation.

definitions.Capital allocation: Funding for long-lived infrastructure rather than routine operating expenses.

options.label: Adopt the performance standard
options.description: Require large buildings to meet phased energy-performance targets.

options.label: Retain voluntary incentives
options.description: Continue rebates and technical assistance without mandatory targets.

packet.status_quo: Large commercial and residential buildings may receive rebates for energy upgrades but face no commonwealth performance requirement.
packet.proposal: Choose whether buildings above fifty thousand square feet must meet gradually tightening energy-use targets over ten years.
packet.who_is_affected: Building owners, tenants, contractors, utilities, and residents affected by energy costs and emissions would be affected.
packet.fiscal_or_operational_effects: Owners would bear upgrade costs and may receive existing rebates. Energy use and utility revenue would likely decline, but the size and timing are uncertain.

arguments_by_option.adopt_standard: A common requirement can produce emissions and energy savings that voluntary programs have not achieved.
arguments_by_option.retain_incentives: Owners face different buildings and financing constraints, and mandates may increase rents or divert capital from other needs.

uncertainties: Future energy prices, financing costs, and the pass-through of upgrade costs to tenants are uncertain.

definitions.Energy-performance target: A limit on measured energy use per unit of building area.

options.label: Create an independent review board
options.description: Authorize a civilian board to investigate serious complaints and publish findings.

options.label: Retain internal and prosecutor review
options.description: Keep complaint investigation with agency professional-standards units and prosecutors.

packet.status_quo: Public safety agencies investigate employee complaints internally, while prosecutors review allegations that may be criminal.
packet.proposal: Choose whether to create an independent civilian board with subpoena authority for serious complaints and public reporting duties.
packet.who_is_affected: Residents filing complaints, public safety employees, agency leaders, prosecutors, and taxpayers would be affected.
packet.fiscal_or_operational_effects: The board would cost an estimated three million dollars annually and could require agencies to provide records and staff time.

arguments_by_option.create_independent_board: Independent investigation can improve accountability and public trust when agencies are accused of misconduct.
arguments_by_option.retain_internal_review: Existing investigators have operational expertise, and an additional board may duplicate work or politicize disciplinary review.

uncertainties: The effect on complaint resolution time, employee retention, and public trust is uncertain.

definitions.Subpoena authority: Legal power to require testimony or production of specified records.

options.label: Unified service portal
options.description: Create one accessible site for applications, renewals, and benefit status.

options.label: Privacy and security upgrades
options.description: Modernize identity controls, encryption, audits, and breach response.

options.label: Public data and transparency
options.description: Publish standardized budgets, contracts, performance measures, and public records.

options.label: Offline and assisted access
options.description: Expand in-person, telephone, language, and disability support alongside digital services.

packet.status_quo: Agencies maintain separate aging systems, and residents often repeat information across services.
packet.proposal: Use a one-hundred-credit quadratic voting budget across four digital-government priorities. Assigning a priority v votes costs v squared credits. The twenty-million-dollar improvement budget would follow the aggregate vote totals.
packet.who_is_affected: Residents using public services, agency employees, vendors, researchers, and people with limited digital access would be affected.
packet.fiscal_or_operational_effects: The total budget is fixed at twenty million dollars. Funding one priority more heavily leaves less capacity for the others.

arguments_by_option.service_portal: A unified portal can reduce repeated paperwork and make services easier to navigate.
arguments_by_option.privacy_security: Security and privacy failures can cause severe individual harm and undermine every digital service.
arguments_by_option.open_data: Consistent public information improves oversight, research, and accountability.
arguments_by_option.offline_access: Modernization should not exclude residents who lack reliable internet, accessible interfaces, language support, or confidence online.

uncertainties: Legacy-system condition and procurement performance may change the cost and delivery time of each priority.

definitions.Quadratic voting credit: The cost unit for expressing support. Assigning v votes to an option costs v squared credits, and unused credits are permitted.
